verdict.rationale: Entrust documents a Known Faces report that compares an applicant's latest captured media against previous applicants in the account database and flags potential repeat identity fraud. That covers the face-resurfacing half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows duplicate detection for documents reused across applicants, and name-mismatch flagging is only implied. missing for 10: duplicate/reused document detection across applicants, explicit flagging of the same identity under different names, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a risk analyst, the platform detects repeat and duplicate identities across verifications — the same face or document resurfacing under different names is flagged automatically

citations.quote: The Known Faces report compares a specific applicant's likeness in their most recently captured media... to media from previous applicants in your Entrust account database... highlighting potential repeat identity fraud attempts
alerts you to faces which have already been through your identity verification flow, highlighting potential repeat identity fraud attempts
